title: Hosted proxy TLS session exhaustion -> 502/504 waves; harmonize retries and connection reuse
creator: Diego Martínez
description: Multiple customers reported recurring 502/504 errors and long tail timeouts during tenant bursts. Initial triage showed disproportionate retries from edge proxies immediately after upstream model-serving node connection resets. Investigation traced the immediate cause to TLS session cache exhaustion on the edge layer combined with upstream model-worker eviction of idle sessions during GC, which triggered connection closures that the proxy retried aggressively. The interaction produced retry amplification and tenant-visible failure waves across Hosted API endpoints.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate a burst of large streaming requests from 50 synthetic tenants over 30s
2) Configure model-serving pool to run aggressive idle eviction (short keepalive/slot recycle)
3) Observe edge proxy logs: connection close events followed by immediate retries and TLS session cache misses
4) Reproduce increased 502/504 rates and long-tail latency on downstream clients
root_cause: Upstream model-serving worker eviction closed connections during ongoing requests while edge proxies retried non-idempotent requests. The edge TLS session cache was sized for steady-state connections; amplified retries caused it to exhaust and fall back to full handshake, increasing CPU and connection churn. No guard existed to block retries for streaming/non-idempotent paths, and connection keepalive reuse was insufficient under churn.
mitigation_plan: Hotpatch edge proxy config to limit retries to 1 for non-idempotent POST/streaming endpoints (deployed 2026-03-10)
Increase edge TLS session cache size and adjust eviction policy to prefer recently-used tenant sessions (temporary)
Enable tenant-scoped circuit breaker to fast-fail with 503 and trigger quieter backoff for tenants exceeding failure thresholds
Add a short client-side guidance notice to SDK docs marking streaming generation as non-retryable until longer-term fixes
Roll out an immediate downstream workaround: auto-slowdown/queue tokens for noisy tenants in Hosted queues
resolution_summary: Hotfix reduced immediate error-wave amplification by enforcing stricter retry limits and tuning TLS session caching. Error rates for impacted tenants dropped from ~18% to ~2% within 30 minutes of hotpatch. Root cause trace shows upstream worker-side idle eviction + proxy retry policy mismatch; a coordinated longer-term change is required in both model-serving keepalive behavior and proxy retry semantics.
implementation_notes: Edge proxy PR: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/4321 - add request metadata to mark non-retryable streaming paths
Runtime PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2119 - defer aggressive idle eviction during rolling upgrades and add telemetry hook
Console change: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/889 - tenant error alerts and per-tenant retry-budget display

acceptance_criteria: Edge retry policy enforces <=1 automatic retry for non-idempotent generation paths
TLS session cache configured to sustain 3x current burst baseline without full-handshake thrash
Per-tenant circuit breaker prevents a noisy tenant from causing cross-tenant amplification
E2E synthetic test reproduces previous failure mode with and without patches and shows improvement >90% reduction in 5xx during burst
postmortem_actions: 1) Instrument per-tenant retry budget and display in Console (owner: Console Eng)
2) Add integration test that simulates upstream CLOSE_DUE_TO_EVICTION and verifies proxy does not amplify retries
3) Update runtime eviction policy: avoid charging active streams; add grace period post-worker-rotation
4) Publish customer-facing KB and proactive alerting for tenants on heavy streaming workloads
5) Schedule follow-up: Dedicated capacity gating to isolate noisy tenants (Q2 initiative)
